models.label: LFP/graphite 250 Ah prismatic
models.structure: Loss grows with time to the power 0.526 (calendar) and with equivalent full cycles to the power 0.828 (cycling): both sublinear, so the curve falls early and then flattens.
models.data: NREL tests on a large commercial prismatic LFP/graphite cell (>250 Ah, energy-to-power 6 per hour). Charging was limited to 0.65 C (0.16 C at 10 degC), so it is only fitted on low-rate data.

models.label: LFP/graphite 3 Ah cylindrical (Sony-Murata)
models.structure: Calendar loss is a saturating sigmoid in time. Cycling loss grows as (rate x cycles) to the power 1.13, slightly faster than linear. A break-in term acts only above 3 full cycles a day, so it is inactive for buses.
models.data: Technical University of Munich tests on Sony-Murata 3 Ah LFP/graphite cylindrical cells (high power, long life). Cycling only at 25 and 45 degC, and no temperature effect on cycling fade because of limited data.

ensemble.scalar_note: This is the default spread in BLAST-Lite's own distribution helper, a convention and not a measured uncertainty.
ensemble.pack_penalty_note: Applied as time compression: pack capacity at time t equals cell capacity at t / (1 - penalty).

limitations: No public LFP bus-pack data exists: nothing in this tool has been validated on buses.
Both ageing models are NREL fits to laboratory tests on one cell design each. Neither has been checked against a battery pack in service.
Both cells were cycled at 80 to 100 % depth of discharge. A bus using about 70 % a day is outside that range, so the cycling term is extrapolated.
The two models differ by roughly 2 to 3 times on calendar ageing. The range shown is that disagreement plus assumed cell-to-cell scatter, not a statistical confidence interval.
The weakest-cell pack penalty (20 to 30 % earlier end of life) follows NREL's rule of thumb. It is an assumption, not data.
Neither model represents a sudden late-life knee: capacity loss never accelerates sharply, so timing near the end of life is likely optimistic.
Cell temperature is air temperature plus an assumed heat rise. Charge power only acts through time spent full; HVAC load and seasonal energy use are not modelled.
BMS-reported state of health is never treated as ground truth, and vendor data may only calibrate.
